reasons: Lake identity gives case_name United States v. Lee, court U.S., date_decided 1927-05-31, and year 1927.
Lake citations list official 274 U.S. 559, parallels 47 S. Ct. 746 and 71 L. Ed. 1202, and vendor-neutral 1927 U.S. LEXIS 52.

defect.evidence_quote: But no search on the high seas is shown. The testimony of the boatswain shows that he used a searchlight. It is not shown that there was any exploration below decks or under hatches. For aught that appears, the cases of liquor were on deck and, like the defendants, were discovered before the motor boat was boarded.
defect.locator_note: holding field; searchlight portion at star page 563 in cached opinion text
defect.problem: The core holding is supported, but the phrasing overstates the searchlight point as a categorical factual finding that the light merely revealed what was already in open view. The opinion is narrower: no search at sea was shown; no below-deck or hatch exploration was shown; and, 'for aught that appears,' the cases were on deck and discovered before boarding.
defect.proposed_fix: Rephrase to say the Court held that, on this record, no search at sea was shown: the searchlight use, with no shown below-deck or hatch exploration and with the cases apparently on deck before boarding, was comparable to marine or field glasses and not constitutionally prohibited. Retain the probable-cause boarding/search/seizure/arrest holding.

reasons: The Coast Guard authority portion is supported by the opinion: officers may board and search such vessels on probable cause to believe they are subject to seizure for revenue-law violations and may arrest persons engaged in such violations.

The searchlight portion is supported only in the opinion's record-dependent terms: no search was shown, and the use of the searchlight was compared to marine or field glasses and held not constitutionally prohibited.
The reversal is supported by the opinion's final disposition: Reversed.
residual_risks: Lake pinpoints are empty; support verification came from the cached full opinion text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Avoid 'merely revealed what was already in open view' unless tied to the opinion's narrower 'for aught that appears' formulation.

defect.problem: The disclosed evidence does not verify the editorial home-role assertion that Lee is 'Key' on the Fourth Amendment Recalibration page. The lake record has no home-role field or supporting taxonomy, and the opinion text supports only the underlying searchlight/probable-cause holdings, not the 'Key' role weight on an external home page.
defect.proposed_fix: Remove or downgrade the Key role unless a disclosed home page, role rubric, or authority record affirmatively supports classifying United States v. Lee as Key for Fourth Amendment Recalibration.

reasons: The content page itself asserts the role, but that is the assertion under review and cannot independently verify the role weight.

The opinion text supports a Fourth Amendment searchlight proposition, but not the editorial judgment that the case is Key within the named home.
residual_risks: An undisclosed home page or taxonomy might support the role, but it is outside the disclosed evidentiary universe.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Treat as Related or supply disclosed role criteria showing why Lee is Key.
